title: 7-year wait for GMC recruitment rules to end in a month: Chief Secretary

ai.summary: Chief Secretary Sajjan Singh Yadav assured protesting employees of five new Government Medical Colleges that their service recruitment rules would be notified within a month, ending a nearly seven-year wait for the rules.

facts.claim: Chief Secretary Sajjan Singh Yadav assured protesting non-gazetted employees of the five newly established Government Medical Colleges (GMCs) that their long-pending service recruitment rules would be notified within a month
facts.quote: Chief Secretary Sajjan Singh Yadav on Tuesday assured protesting non-gazetted employees of the five newly established Government Medical Colleges (GMCs) that their long-pending service recruitment rules would be notified within a month, raising hopes of ending a nearly seven-year wait.

facts.claim: The employees have been protesting the delay in framing and notifying their service recruitment rules, alleging that the absence of these rules has stalled their career progression and promotions
facts.quote: The employees have been protesting the delay in framing and notifying their service recruitment rules, alleging that the absence of these rules has stalled their career progression and promotions.

facts.claim: Protests are underway at all five newly established medical colleges — GMC Doda, GMC Rajouri, GMC Anantnag, GMC Baramulla and GMC Kathua
facts.quote: Protests are underway at all five newly established medical colleges — GMC Doda, GMC Rajouri, GMC Anantnag, GMC Baramulla and GMC Kathua.

facts.claim: The paramedical employees had earlier observed a three-day strike from November 16 to 19, while employees at GMC Rajouri have continued their protest for the past nine days
facts.quote: The paramedical employees had earlier observed a three-day strike from November 16 to 19, while employees at GMC Rajouri have continued their protest for the past nine days.

facts.claim: During their interaction with the Chief Secretary, the employees said they had received repeated assurances over the past seven years, including a deadline to complete the process by September 30, 2026, but no concrete action had followed
facts.quote: During their interaction with the Chief Secretary, the employees said they had received repeated assurances over the past seven years, including a deadline to complete the process by September 30, 2026, but no concrete action had followed.

facts.claim: The Chief Secretary said he assumed charge only three days ago but was aware of the issue and had already taken it up with the Secretary of the Health and Medical Education Department
facts.quote: The Chief Secretary said he assumed charge only three days ago but was aware of the issue and had already taken it up with the Secretary of the Health and Medical Education Department.

facts.claim: He informed the employees that the recruitment rules had been forwarded by the Health and Medical Education Department to the Finance Department
facts.quote: He informed the employees that the recruitment rules had been forwarded by the Health and Medical Education Department to the Finance Department.

facts.claim: The proposal would subsequently require clearance from other concerned departments, including the Administrative Reforms and Inspections (ARI) and Trainings Department, before submission to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for final approval
facts.quote: The proposal would subsequently require clearance from other concerned departments, including the Administrative Reforms and Inspections (ARI) and Trainings Department, before submission to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for final approval.

facts.claim: Yadav said he would convene a meeting of the concerned officers within the next 24 hours to expedite the approval process. "I will make every effort to complete the entire process within one month and put the case before the Lieutenant Governor for approval," he assured the employees
facts.quote: Yadav said he would convene a meeting of the concerned officers within the next 24 hours to expedite the approval process. "I will make every effort to complete the entire process within one month and put the case before the Lieutenant Governor for approval," he assured the employees.

ai.background_note: Protests by non-gazetted employees of five new Government Medical Colleges over delayed service recruitment rules, which have stalled their career progression and affected healthcare delivery.
